title: Pinned–pinned column, Euler buckling
sentence: A 200 × 200 mm S355 column, 5 m between pins, modelled as its lower half with a symmetry plane at mid-height — one linear buckling Step against π²EI/L².

expected.reference: Euler P_cr = π²EI/(KL)² with K = 1 and I = b⁴/12; the eigenvalue multiplies the 40 kN reference load

theory: A linear buckling Step solves $(K + \lambda K_g)\varphi = 0$: $\lambda$ is the factor on the applied load at which the structure has a second equilibrium shape. With a 1 MPa reference pressure on a 40 000 mm² section the reference load is 40 kN, so $P_{cr} = 40\lambda$ kN. The closed form is $P_{cr} = \pi^2 EI/(KL)^2$ with $K = 1$ for pinned–pinned. This eigenvalue is an **upper bound**, not a design load: it assumes a perfectly straight, residual-stress-free, elastic member. EN 1993-1-1 §6.3.1 replaces it with $N_{b,Rd} = \chi A f_y/\gamma_{M1}$, and here the curve-c value is about 60 % of the eigenvalue.
